proof_attempt_summary: The discovery run derived a rare-event finite minimax branch and attempted an unequal-interior Poisson allocation certificate and finite transfer. The field-tier review assigned an incremental ceiling, and the math panel left the load-bearing Bernstein-box certificate unreproduced along with three positioning or presentation findings. This administrative failed bank records an unverified below-floor package; it does not assert that the mathematical claim was refuted.
tldr: Routine outcome codes are observed for every randomized participant, but costly chart review is needed to find rare events hidden among coded negatives. Under perfect positive predictive value, known arm-specific code rates, and a common false-negative ceiling, the average-treatment-effect correction is a signed contrast of two bounded binomial probabilities. The project characterizes the all-estimator finite-sample game for deterministic and randomized audit allocations, proves exact one-arm concentration in the rare region, transfers the allocation landscape to a continuous bounded-Poisson experiment when \(B\varepsilon\to c\), certifies an unequal-interior phase, and reconnects the game to regular two-phase variance allocation as \(c\to\infty\). The open kernel is the complete least-favorable-support and allocation-contact phase diagram.
gap: Scalar restricted-binomial theory identifies boundary-supported least-favorable priors, and regular validation-design theory optimizes asymptotic variance. Neither determines the all-estimator risk of a signed two-arm bounded-rate correction under one hard audit budget, nor the boundary-to-interior allocation transition when expected audit discoveries remain finite.
fill: The paper supplies finite-sample saddle representations and rare-region formulas, an explicit binomial-to-Poisson risk comparison, a certified unequal-interior Poisson comparison, a regular-limit converse, and a concrete outward-certified handle for the full allocation frontier.
